definition: A version of the game of baggataway, in which two teams of players use long-handled, racketlike implements (crosses) to catch, carry, or throw a ball down the field or into the opponents’ goal. The goal is defined by uprights and a crossbar framing a loose net. The distinctive feature of the game is the crosse (lacrosse stick), the implement used by the players to carry, catch, and pass the ball. The crosse is sharply bent at the top to form a hook from the end of which a thong is drawn and fastened to the shaft about 2 or 3 feet from the end of the handle, forming an oval triangle that is woven with a loose network of leather, nylon, or gut to form the pocket with which the ball is handled.(from https://www.britannica.com/sports/lacrosse)
name: Lacrosse

definition: The field of physics that explains how extremely small objects simultaneously have the characteristics of both particles (tiny pieces of matter) and waves (a disturbance or variation that transfers energy).
name: Quantum Mechanics

definition: Short summaries of research articles written in clear, easy-to-understand language, intended to be a useful way of communicating health research to a non-expert reader.
name: Plain Language Summaries

definition: The ability to effectively adapt one's cognitive and behavioral strategies in response to changing task or environmental demands. (from Clinical Psychology Review August 2021,102061).
name: Cognitive Flexibility

definition: Mixing of several samples together in a batch or pooled sample, then testing the pooled sample with a diagnostic test. This approach increases the number of individuals that can be tested using the same amount of resources.(CDRH-EUA-Templates@fda.hhs.gov)
name: Pooled Testing

definition: Health care professionals who render service or treatment, under the direction of or in collaboration with a physician, in accordance with their education and training and State statutes, rules and regulations. Services provided are related to injury and illness prevention, wellness promotion and education, emergent care, examination and clinical diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, and rehabilitation of injuries and medical conditions. (from https://www.bocatc.org/)
name: Athletic Trainers

definition: A discipline designed to study research itself and its practices. To promote robust science, meta-research uses an interdisciplinary approach to examine research practices with the same scientific rigor given to other areas of scientific inquiry. The objective of this approach is to understand and improve how research is performed, communicated, verified, evaluated, and de-incentivized.
name: Meta-Research

definition: Healthcare pricing information provided in advance of receiving care and publicizing how and from whom patients can obtain price estimates. Hospitals operating in the United States are required to make public a list of standard charges for items and services they provide. (Federal Register 84 FR 65524)
name: Price Transparency

definition: A behavioral mechanism between depression and development of obesity and abdominal obesity. Moreover, adults with a combination of shorter night sleep duration and higher emotional eating may be particularly vulnerable to weight gain. (Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act . 2019 Mar 20;16(1):28.)
name: Emotional Eating

definition: Machines that are engineered to learn about their environment and make decisions to complete tasks with little to no human intervention. These robots may be designed to complete tasks such as patient intervention, remote monitoring, inventory transportation, among many others.
name: Autonomous Robots

definition: Technological systems that perform automated tasks within specific environments enabled by artificial intelligence.
name: Intelligent Systems

definition: A form of ensemble learning methods which combines weak learners to create strong ones, which reduces training errors and bias in the training models. There are different types of boosting such as gradient boosting, XGBoost, and Adaboost.
name: Boosting Machine Learning Algorithms

definition: A machine learning process used to reduce the number of attributes or features of data (called dimensionality) thereby simplifying understanding of the dataset without a loss in data integrity.
name: Dimensionality Reduction

definition: A method in machine learning where several base learners are combined to create an optimal learning model. This can be used for a variety of models including forecasting, classification, or function approximation.
name: Ensemble Learning

definition: A machine learning training method in which an agent in an uncertain environment is rewarded for optimal behaviors and punished for undesired behaviors, allowing the agent to learn from trial-and-error.
name: Reinforcement Machine Learning

aliases: Particle Swarm Optimization with Time Varying Acceleration Coefficient
PSO with Time Varying Acceleration Coefficient
definition: A heuristic computational algorithm designed to find optimal solutions in a random search space. Particle swarm optimization measures swarm intelligence which is a computation measurement inspired by behaviors of self-organized swarming animals.
name: Particle Swarm Optimization

definition: The process of recognizing and extracting meaningful information from patterns in data. Pattern analysis in machine learning is often used for predictions and forecasting.
name: Pattern Analysis, Machine

definition: Artificial neural networks designed to automatically learn features through the use of sequence of layers which transform one volume to the next. Convolutional neural networks initially produce a feature map by use of convolution layers consisting of a set of learnable filters convolved with input, i.e., having smaller widths and heights and the same depth as that of input volume.
name: Convolutional Neural Networks

definition: A form of recurrent computer neural networks which allows for important information to be retained and less important information to be erased. These kinds of networks are used for tasks such as language translation, anomaly detection, speech and handwriting recognition, and time series prediction.
name: Long Short Term Memory

definition: A network where information is only passed in one direction. This is the opposite of a recurrent neural network, in which information is processed in a cycle.
name: Feedforward Neural Networks

definition: A feedforward neural network designed with a single layer hidden node where the weights between inputs and hidden nodes are randomly assigned. Extreme learning machines can be trained fast and used for the data clustering, grouping, regression, prediction, and forecasting.
name: Extreme Learning Machines

definition: A feedforward neural network with multiple layers, an input layer, at least three hidden layers, and an output layer, generally used for pattern recognition and classification.
name: Multilayer Perceptrons

definition: Neural networks designed to process signals supported on graphs.
name: Graph Neural Networks

definition: A three-layer neural network made of an input layer, hidden layer, and output layer. Radial basis function networks are used for function approximation, interpolation, classification, and time series prediction.
name: Radial Basis Function Networks

definition: A type of neural network where the output from the previous step is fed as input to the current step with the help of a hidden layer which tracks data sequences. Recurrent neural network is often used when the data is sequential, and weights need to be treated same across all the layers such as in time series data and speech recognition. Variation of recurrent neural network include bidirectional neural network and long short-term memory.
name: Recurrent Neural Networks

definition: Fully interconnected, single layer neural network, which can be used for associative memory and optimization tasks.
name: Hopfield Neural Networks

definition: Algorithms designed to solve a problem by modifying their behaviors when facing with an unseen task with limited data during training.
name: Adaptive Algorithms

definition: An unsupervised learning network which is composed of two separate networks, a generator which produces content and a discriminator which works to identify real content from the generated content. Over time, generative adversarial networks create data that increasingly resembles the input data.
name: Generative Adversarial Networks

definition: A class of algorithms that predicts which category an observation belongs based on training data.
name: Classification Algorithms

definition: Algorithms designed to find groups of similar data points (called clusters) in the dataset. Clustering is often used for feature engineering or pattern discovery in unsupervised machine learning.
name: Clustering Algorithms

definition: A class of algorithms which both reduces and restores the size of files to increase their portability. Compression algorithms can be lossy or lossless.
name: Compression Algorithms

definition: Dynamic programming is an optimization technique where smaller portions of problems are broken down, solved, and remembered, in order to solve a larger and more complex problem.
name: Dynamic Programming

definition: Heuristic search algorithms which direct the random searches to the area of better performance or fitness function by computationally creating the conditions inspired by NATURAL SELECTION. They are commonly used to generate solutions for optimization problems.
name: Genetic Algorithms

definition: A class of algorithms which enables a computer to learn as it goes, thereby accomplishing its goal without being explicitly programmed to do so.
name: Machine Learning Algorithms

definition: An unsupervised learning technique where the machine learns patterns in unlabeled data sets, makes compressed representations and reconstructs the input as output at minimum loss of features from the input. Autoencoders are useful in denoising images, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION and feature extraction.
name: Autoencoder

definition: Finite learnable stochastic models often used in MACHINE LEARNING consisting of two processes: a MARKOV CHAIN and an event observed and analyzed in a state unknown or hidden to the observer. Hidden Markov Models are often used in BIOINFORMATICS, time series analysis and speech and handwriting recognition.
name: Hidden Markov Models

definition: Weakly supervised learning algorithms where training set is arranged in a labeled bag of instances, and a single class label is assigned to a bag.
name: Multiple-Instance Learning Algorithms

definition: Overwhelming and persistent reluctance to go to school, which usually occurs during the primary school years and is often a symptom of an educational, social, or emotional problem. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology)
name: Phobia, School

definition: A type of TELEMEDICINE in which healthcare providers monitor patients using digital medical devices. Data collected from these devices are then electronically transferred to providers for care management and has been used to measure symptoms of chronic conditions, such as cardiac diseases, diabetes, and asthma. Benefits include patient engagement, patient adherence to their treatment plan, and the ability to expand physician reach and easily provide care to patients without the need for patients in person encounters. (From https://psnet.ahrq.gov/perspective/remote-patient-monitoring. Accessed 11 Nov 2023)
name: Remote Patient Monitoring

definition: The subjective perception and evaluation of one’s own body in terms of different aspects such as size, shape, musculature or muscle tone, weight, and fitness.
name: Body Satisfaction

definition: Rehabilitation treatment following an ischemic stroke where patients suffer from muscular weakness or paralysis on one side.It is also used as a therapy for children with cerebral palsy.
name: Constraint Induced Movement Therapy

definition: Professionals trained in the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.
name: Psychologists

definition: Authorization allowing the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to strengthen public health protections against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats including infectious diseases, by facilitating the availability and use of medical countermeasures needed during public health emergencies. Under section 564 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, FDA may authorize unapproved medical products or unapproved uses of approved medical products to be used in an emergency to diagnose, treat, or prevent serious or life-threatening diseases or agents when certain criteria are met, including there are no adequate, approved, and available alternatives.(From fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/emergency-use-authorization-medical-products-and-related-authorities)
name: Emergency Use Authorization

definition: Removal of the TRACHEOSTOMY tube.
name: Tracheostomy Decannulation

aliases: Cardiovascular Implantable Electronic Device Lead Extraction
definition: Removal of electronic wire lead(s) of IMPLANTED ELECTRODES, e.g., implanted ARTIFICIAL PACEMAKER or IMPLANTABLE CARDIOVERTER DEFIBRILLATOR.
name: Device Lead Extraction

definition: Surgical removal of devices, including BONE SCREWS, pins, BONE PLATES, and wires used in FRACTURE FIXATION. Hardwares in general refer to non-electrical devices, most often orthopedic, and are removed due to infection, malfunction and to allow proper growth.
name: Hardware Removal

definition: Meningitis caused by a fungus of the genus COCCIDIOIDES, endemic to the SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES, south-central Washington State, and parts of Mexico and Central and South America.
name: Coccidioidal Meningitis

definition: Congenital vascular malformation where the portal venous system blood (PORTAL SYSTEM) bypasses the liver sinusoids and drains into the systemic vein through a shunt.
name: Congenital Portosystemic Shunt

aliases: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Autoantibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein-Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder
definition: A disease in which serum antibodies are directed against MYELIN-OLIGODENDROCYTE GLYCOPROTEIN. MOGAD is typically associated with ACUTE DISSEMINATED ENCEPHALOMYELITIS; NEUROMYELITIS OPTICA; or TRANSVERSE MYELITIS.
name: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease

definition: INTERLEUKINS that affect the differentiation and function of LYMPHOCYTES and MYELOID CELLS and regulate both IMMUNITY, INNATE and ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY. They are also involved in the expansion of NK CELLS.
name: Interleukin-21

definition: A Pentosyltransferase involved in the catabolism of QUINOLINIC ACID, NAD+ biosynthesis, and APOPTOSIS.
name: Nicotinate-Nucleotide Diphosphorylase (Carboxylating)

definition: A blowfly species in the genus Lucilia. Lucilia sericata is the most often used species for MAGGOT THERAPY and is responsible for sheep blowfly strike (MYIASIS) in northern Europe. Can form hybrids with Australian sheep blowfly, LUCILIA CUPRINA.
name: Lucilia sericata

definition: A blowfly species in the genus Lucilia. Lucilia cuprina is responsible for sheep blowfly strike (MYIASIS) in Australia. Can form hybrids with LUCILIA SERICATA.
name: Lucilia cuprina

definition: One of the main brain dopaminergic circuits, which connects the MIDBRAIN with the LIMBIC SYSTEM, going from the VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA to the NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS, connecting with other structures such as the AMYGDALA and the PREFRONTAL CORTEX.
name: Mesolimbic System

definition: Fitness professionals who work with people to identify and achieve their personal fitness and health goals. They create exercise programs and motivate clients through feedback and accountability.
name: Personal Trainers

definition: The Gilbert Islands were granted self-rule by the UK in 1971 and complete independence in 1979 under the new name of Kiribati.
name: Kiribati

definition: Review to identify knowledge gaps, scope a body of literature, clarify concepts or to investigate research conduct.
name: Scoping Review

definition: A functional gene designed for targeted delivery to specific tissues within the body for correcting or repairing a gene that may be defective.
name: Gene Therapy Agents

definition: Information or entertainment in digital form, especially online via the Internet. Examples of digital media include online news sources, video games, blogs, and social media. The term may also be used to describe online content, especially content that is interactive; on-demand media that is accessible through a range of devices; and media that is responded to or shared in real time. It is sometimes used to refer to content that is created, published, or distributed by individuals or non-traditional publishers, such as bloggers.
name: Digital Media

definition: A laboratory technique for determining the DNA sequence of an organism's genome. In this approach, DNA of an organism is randomly broken into small DNA fragments which are then sequenced individually. Computational methods are then utilized to reassemble these sequenced fragments accurately, reconstructing the complete genome sequence.
name: Shotgun Sequencing

aliases: Dynamic Susceptibility Contrast Perfusion Weighted Imaging
Arterial Spin Labeling Perfusion Weighted Imaging
definition: A specialized type of MRI technique that provides information about HEMODYNAMIC parameters such as CEREBRAL BLOOD VOLUME, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW, and transit time. In perfusion MRI, an exogenous CONTRAST AGENT is usually injected to provide superior tissue contrast and easy delineation of perfusion abnormalities. Endogenous markers can also be used.
name: Perfusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging

definition: A common complication of SICKLE CELL DISEASE arises when MICROVESSELS become obstructed by sickled red blood cells, leading to tissue and organ oxygen deprivation, resulting in acute episodes of pain.
name: Vaso-Occlusive Crises

definition: Uncontrolled anxiety or excessive worry that exceeds the realistic scope of life situations and endures for at least a month or longer.
name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder

definition: A skin condition, typically emerges suddenly and frequently occurs after an infection such as STREPTOCOCCAL INFECTION. While prevalent among children, it can also manifest in young adults. Its defining feature is the eruption of small, red, scaly patches that typically appear on the arms, legs, and torso.
name: Guttate Psoriasis

definition: pain originating from the disrupted function of pain-related sensory pathways in both the periphery and central nervous system (CNS), leading to heightened sensitivity.
name: Nociplastic Pain

definition: An actin-associated protein expressed in platelets and various cells and tissues. It is also recognized as a substrate for CYCLIC GMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES and CYCLIC AMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES. It plays a role in various processes, including platelet activation and cell migration.
name: Vasodilator-Stimulated Phosphoprotein

definition: A class of phenolic compounds that are derived from DIPHENYLMETHANE, 4,4'-dihydroxy-2,2-diphenylpropane, DIPHENYL SULFONE, and their related compounds with similar structures. They are commonly used in the production of POLYMERS.
name: Bisphenols

aliases: Grocery and General Merchandise Store Cashiers
definition: These include (but are not limited to) health care workers, protective service workers (police and EMS), cashiers in grocery and general merchandise stores, production and food processing workers, janitors and maintenance workers, agricultural workers, and truck drivers. (cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/ECIW_4.0_Guidance_on_Essential_Critical_Infrastructure_Workers_Final3_508_0.pdf)
name: Frontline Workers

definition: An iron exporter protein that transports iron from inside of a cell to the outside.
name: Ferroportin

definition: A transcription factor of the T-box family of transcription factors, functions in immune system regulation, particularly in T-cell differentiation. It also is involved in the development of Th1 cells and the regulation of CXCR3 expression.
name: T-bet Transcription Factor

definition: Family of steroid receptors that transport CHOLESTEROL and PHOSPHOLIPIDS. They act as a sensor or transporter of these ligands at contact sites of two different cellular membranes where they function as lipid exchangers, mediating counter-directional transport of two different lipid ligands.
name: Oxysterol Binding Proteins

definition: Polymeric substances that include repeating carbonate molecules in their structure.
name: Polycarbonates

definition: A CYTIDINE DEAMINASE required for several crucial steps of B Cell terminal differentiation.
name: AICDA (Activation-Induced Cytidine Deaminase)

definition: TFIII transcription factor that consists of TFIIIC1 (MW appx 200 kDA) and TFIIIC2 (MW 400-500 kDa) subunits. TFIIIC2 contains the TFIIIC90 subunit, which has HISTONE ACETYLTRANSFERASE activity.
name: Transcription Factor TFIIIC

definition: An artificial intelligence (AI) technique that generates synthetic artifacts by analyzing training examples; learning their patterns and distribution; and then creating realistic facsimiles. It uses generative modeling and advances in deep learning to produce diverse content at scale by utilizing existing media such as text, graphics, audio, and video. (From Association for Computing Machinery, https://doi.org/10.1145/3626110)
name: Generative Artificial Intelligence

definition: Concept that the origins of lifestyle-related disease is formed at the time of fertilization, embryonic, fetal, and neonatal stages by the interrelation between genes and the environments (nutrition, stress, or environmental chemicals). (J Cardiol 2020 Jul;76(1):14-17)...
name: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease

definition: A child or adolescent without the presence of a legal guardian.
name: Unaccompanied Minors

definition: Molecules that include CARBON, BORON and HYDROGEN and typically form into a polygonal structure.
name: Carboranes

definition: A cell-surface mucin-like glycoprotein that is encoded by the PDPN gene and is commonly found in the PULMONARY ALVEOLI, HEART, and endothelium of lymphatic vessels. It interacts with the C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2), expressed on BLOOD PLATELETS. It may also function in TUMOR development and progression.
name: Podoplanin

definition: A nonfamilial polyposis syndrome that is characterized by the presence of diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis, skin hyperpigmentation, ALOPECIA; DIARRHEA, and PROTEIN-LOSING ENTEROPATHY. It was first reported by Cronkhite and Canada in 1955.
name: Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome

aliases: Long Chain Fatty Acid CoA Ligase
Very Long Chain Fatty Acid Acyl-CoA Synthetase
Very Long Chain Fatty Acid Acyl CoA Synthetase
Very Long Chain Acyl CoA Synthetase
definition: Coenzyme A ligase that catalyzes the activation of fatty acids in LIPOGENESIS and membrane remodeling. Activity is independent of PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINES.
name: Long-Chain-Fatty-Acid-CoA Ligase

definition: All of the microbial organisms that naturally exist upon the EPIDERMIS.
name: Skin Microbiome

definition: ECOSYSTEM or ground next to the water between the high tide point and the low tide point.
name: Seashore

definition: Types of THROMBOSPONDINS that regulate the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY.
name: R-Spondins

definition: A T-box transcription factor which regulates the expression of genes required for MESODERM formation and differentiation.
name: Brachyury Protein

definition: A rare, malignant MELANOMA arising from the melanocytes of the UVEA.
name: Uveal Melanoma

definition: A minimally invasive water ablation procedure used for treating BENIGN PROSTATE HYPERPLASIA. During this procedure, a robotically controlled water jet is used to remove excess prostate tissue.
name: Aquablation

definition: Treatment that helps a person work through a greater than normal reaction to a loss, such as the death of a loved one. Therapy may be individual or group therapy.
name: Grief Therapy

definition: Disease that affects linguistic, VISUAL SPATIAL PROCESSING; EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, and MOOD regulation. Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome is associated with acquired lesions in the CEREBELLUM particularly in the posterior lobe and the vermis.
name: Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome

definition: Infection of the lungs in a patient who is not hospitalized or who has not resided in a long-term care facility for 14 days prior to the onset of symptoms. It is associated with some signs and symptoms of acute infection and is accompanied by the presence of an acute infiltrate on chest radiograph.(US Pharm. 2007;32(10):44-5 https://www.uspharmacist.com/article/community-acquired-pneumonia)
name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia

definition: The collection, transformation, and organization of data in order to draw conclusions, make predictions, and drive informed decision making. The process deduces logical sets and patterns by filtering and applying required transformations and models of raw data.
name: Data Analytics

definition: Molecular probes that respond to specific chemical interactions by altering the degree or frequency of their fluorescence. They are used to provide direct visualization of chemical changes within cells.
name: Fluorescent Chemosensor Compounds

definition: Rare abnormality where a fetal part of an identical twin that stopped developing during gestation is found within a normally developing fetus. It is considered a TWIN PREGNANCY complication.
name: Fetus-in-Fetu

definition: The Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended, defines an HBCU as: “…any historically black college or university that was established prior to 1964, whose principal mission was, and is, the education of black Americans, and that is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency or association determined by the Secretary [of Education] to be a reliable authority as to the quality of training offered or is, according to such an agency or association, making reasonable progress toward accreditation.” (https://sites.ed.gov/whhbcu/one-hundred-and-five-historically-black-colleges-and-universities/
name: Historically Black Colleges and Universities

definition: The use of drugs to enhance or sustain sexual activity primarily but not exclusively by men who have sex with men.
name: Chemsex

definition: A rare congenital malformation that affects the development of the urinary, digestive, and REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS due to CLOACA malformations. In this condition, the large intestine develops outside the abdominal cavity, with the bladder connected to it. Due to this abnormal connection between the colon and the bladder, urine and stool can mix, and there is often no anus.
name: Cloacal Exstrophy

definition: Technicians who follow prescriptions for visual correction, order lenses, and dispense eyeglasses and contact lenses.
name: Opticians

definition: Perception or feeling of control over one's own actions thereby influencing the course of events and outcomes. SELF-EFFICACY on the other hand is beliefs or expectations in self-ability to achieve intended goals or to produce a given effect in specific tasks.
name: Sense of Agency

definition: A therapeutic intervention designed to improve PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING through reduced ANXIETY; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; DISTRESS and improved mood by increased mindfulness.
name: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction

definition: Persistent and difficult to control psychological distress over CLIMATE CHANGE.
name: Climate Anxiety

definition: Death of a pregnant or birthing person during pregnancy or up to one year after the end of pregnancy from health issues related to pregnancy.
name: Pregnancy-Related Death

definition: The practice of medicine concerned with conditions in individuals resulting from exposure to environments where the ambient pressure is increased, such as the undersea environment.
name: Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine

definition: Corticotropin Releasing Hormone Receptor 1 is a G protein coupled receptor that binds corticotropin-releasing hormone, a peptide that plays a key role in activating signal transduction pathways involved in the stress response.
name: CRF Receptor, Type 1

definition: A multifunctional protein primarily found in the PLASMA with His/Pro-Rich (HRR) region which contains approximately 12 tandem internal repeats of the 5-residue G[H/P][H/P]PH consensus sequence. Histidine-rich glycoprotein has a diverse range of ligands that are involved in many biological processes, including COAGULATION; IMMUNE RESPONSE; ANGIOGENESIS, and WOUND HEALING.
name: Histidine-Rich Glycoprotein

definition: Outcome anticipated or expected due to various qualities of a healthcare treatment.
name: Treatment Expectations

definition: A healthcare framework that typically integrates clinical information systems to improve CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING, support for COMMUNITY RESOURCES and SELF-MANAGEMENT and improvement of care continuity through better delivery system design and organization.
name: Chronic Care Model

definition: A bifunctional glycosyltransferase involved in transferring GLUCURONIC ACID and N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in the gene EXT1, coding for this protein (as well as mutations in other genes), are responsible for defects in heparan sulfate synthesis resulting in HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES. Exostosin-1, along with EXOSTOSIN-2, is a component of heparan sulfate polymerase.
name: Exostosin 1

definition: Various measurements of proper patient compliance in medication adherence. Adherence measurement includes self-reporting forms and monitoring systems and devices used for assessing medication adherence.
name: Assessment of Medication Adherence

definition: Various interventions designed to improve MEDICATION ADHERENCE often overcoming barriers to PATIENT COMPLIANCE.
name: Adherence Interventions

aliases: Omphalocele Exstrophy Imperforate Anus Spinal Defects Complex
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Bladder, Imperforate Anus, Spinal Abnormalities
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Cloaca, Imperforate Anus, and Spinal Defects
definition: A combination of defects comprising OMPHALOCELE, exstrophy of the cloaca, ANUS IMPERFORATE, and spinal defects. This rare complex is thought to represent the most severe end of a spectrum of birth defects, the exstrophy-epispadias sequence, which, in order of increasing severity, includes phallic separation with EPISPADIAS, pubic diastasis, EXSTROPHY OF THE BLADDER, and CLOACAL EXSTROPHY. (From OMIM 258040)
name: OEIS Complex

definition: Loss of the MAXILLA bone mass and/or height due to natural edentulous maxilla (JAW, EDENTULOUS) or previous dental extractions. It may require a reconstruction via BONE TRANSPLANTATION and/or ALVEOLOPLASTY prior to a DENTAL IMPLANTATION.
name: Atrophic Maxilla

aliases: Agranular CD4+ CD56+ Hematodermic Neoplasm Tumor
Agranular CD4+ Natural Killer Cell Leukemia
definition: A rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy derived from the precursors of PLASMACYTOID DENDRITIC CELLS. Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasms affect bone marrow and blood in addition to the lymph nodes, spleen, central nervous system, and skin.
name: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm

definition: Allergic reaction to certain foods, including fresh fruits, vegetables and nuts which share CROSS REACTIONS to allergens from trees, grass or pollens. Oral allergy syndrome is limited to itchy lips, mouth, and throat without severe ANAPHYLAXIS and is often associated with chronic EOSINOPHILIC ESOPHAGITIS.
name: Oral Allergy Syndrome

aliases: Return of Research Results to Study Participants
definition: The return of individual results involves the return of information specific to the research subject. It encompasses information that is linked to the identity of a research subject and pertains to that subject and the focus of the study. Individual results can be obtained in clinical, social behavioral, and other types of research is not limited to clinical research (https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/sachrp-committee/recommendations/attachment-b-return-individual-research-results/index.html).
name: Return of Individual Research Results

definition: Co-occurrence of DIABETES MELLITUS and OBESITY largely due to diabetic complication from HYPERGLYCEMIA. Diabesity is also associated with faster deterioration of diabetic symptoms and complications.
name: Diabesity

definition: Generally an issue or an institution emerging into the sphere of politics such as making previously unpolitical matters political. (Tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/13501763.2019.1619188)
name: Politicization

definition: A way of referring people to non-clinical local services (for example, sports activities, arts, group learning, community-based activities, cookery and gardening), with the sole aim of ensuring human contact, followed by support and care.
name: Social Prescribing

definition: Surface-active substances produced by plants and microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and yeast. They have the ability to reduce surface and INTERFACIAL TENSION, making them useful in a variety of applications.
name: Biosurfactants

definition: A process where chemical reactions are carried out in a continuously flowing stream rather than in batch production.
name: Continuous Flow Chemistry

definition: The clinical application of SYSTEMS BIOLOGY, that focuses on identifying the underlying drivers of a patient's disease and addressing, through personalized therapeutic interventions, those root causes of the disease.
name: Functional Medicine

definition: A left-handed conformation of double stranded RNA that is similar in structure to Z-DNA.
name: RNA, Z-Form

definition: A portable imaging device used to perform radiographic examinations outside the traditional radiology department. Mobile X-ray machines provide diagnostic imaging when patients cannot be easily moved or in locations that lack permanent imaging facilities.
name: Portable X-Ray

definition: Digital certificates, in the form of data recorded on a BLOCKCHAIN, that signify ownership of associated digital items, such as images, music, or videos, not contained in the certificate data itself.
name: Non-Fungible Tokens

aliases: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older
definition: Pregnancy in women at least 35 years old at the time of delivery. This was formerly known as geriatric pregnancy.
name: Advanced Maternal Age

definition: A rare form of dilated cardiomyopathy which causes heart enlargement and weakness during the last month of pregnancy or within five months of delivery.
name: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy

definition: The facilitation of verbal communication to assist in the healthcare process, by converting a message in one language to the same message in another language.
name: Medical Interpreting

definition: To continue to live in one's home safely, independently, and comfortably in a familiar environment..
name: Aging in Place

definition: Works consisting of meta-analysis of randomized trials in which estimates of comparative treatment effects are visualized and interpreted from a network of interventions that may or may not have been evaluated directly against each other. Common considerations in network meta-analysis include conceptual and statistical heterogeneity and incoherence.
name: Network Meta-Analysis
